functions.name: Observations
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(Y, [Filter],
  LET(
    filt_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    ROWS(FILTER(Y, filt_arg))
  ))

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: n — count of rows used in the regression as a scalar integer
functions.description:
n (number of observations) is the count of data points available to the model after any filtering is applied. It is the fundamental sample size that drives all degrees-of-freedom calculations.

Returns ROWS(FILTER(Y, filt_arg)). X_s is not required because row count is fully determined by Y.

functions.name: DF_Regression
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s,
  COLUMNS(X_s))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

functions.yields: df_regression (k, number of predictors) as a scalar integer
functions.description:
df_regression is the number of degrees of freedom attributable to the regression model — equal to k, the number of predictor columns. The intercept term (if any) is not counted here; it is accounted for implicitly in df_total.

Returns COLUMNS(X_s). Filter and Allow_Intercept do not affect this value.

functions.name: DF_Total
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    n,         Observations(Y, filt_arg),
    IF(allow_arg, n - 1, n)
  ))

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: df_total (n-1 with intercept, n without) as a scalar integer
functions.description:
df_total is the total degrees of freedom for the sum of squares. When an intercept is fit (default), one df is spent estimating the grand mean, giving n - 1. When the model is forced through the origin (Allow_Intercept = FALSE), no df is spent on the mean, giving n. df_total partitions into df_regression + df_residual.

Calls Observations() for n, then returns IF(allow_arg, n-1, n).

functions.name: R_squared
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    INDEX(LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, TRUE), 3, 1)
  ))

arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: R² (coefficient of determination) as a scalar in [0, 1]
functions.description:
R² (coefficient of determination) is the proportion of variance in Y explained by the regression model. It equals SS_regression / SS_total, ranges from 0 (no explanatory power) to 1 (perfect fit), and is the square of Multiple R.

Returns INDEX(LINEST(...), 3, 1) directly. R_squared is the base statistic from which Multiple_R and Adjusted_R2 are derived.

functions.name: DF_Residual
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    DF_Total(Y, allow_arg, filt_arg) - DF_Regression(X_s)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: df_residual (n-k-1 with intercept, n-k without) as a scalar integer
functions.description:
df_residual (also called df_error) is the degrees of freedom remaining after the regression model has been fit. With an intercept it equals n - k - 1; without an intercept it equals n - k. It is the denominator degrees of freedom for the F-test and the penalty term in Adjusted R².

Computed as DF_Total(...) - DF_Regression(...), inheriting the Allow_Intercept correction from DF_Total.

functions.name: Multiple_R
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    SQRT(R_squared(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg))
  ))

arguments.name: Y

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: Multiple R (correlation coefficient) as a scalar in [0, 1]
functions.description:
Multiple R is the Pearson correlation between the observed values of Y and the values predicted by the regression model. It ranges from 0 (no linear relationship) to 1 (perfect linear fit) and is the square root of R².

Computed as SQRT(R_squared(...)).

functions.name: Adjusted_R2
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    1 - (1 - R_squared(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg))
      * DF_Total(Y, allow_arg, filt_arg)
      / DF_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: Adjusted R² as a scalar, typically in [0, 1] but can be negative
functions.description:
Adjusted R² penalises R² for the number of predictors relative to sample size, correcting for the inflation that occurs when irrelevant predictors are added. It equals 1 - (1 - R²) × df_total / df_residual, which reduces to the familiar 1 - (1 - R²)(n-1)/(n-k-1) when an intercept is fit. Unlike R² it can decrease when a predictor adds less explanatory power than expected by chance, and can be negative when the model fits worse than a horizontal line.

Computed as 1 - (1 - R_squared(...)) * DF_Total(...) / DF_Residual(...), inheriting the Allow_Intercept correction from both df functions.

functions.name: SS_Total
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    y_filt, FILTER(Y, filt_arg),
    IF(allow_arg, DEVSQ(y_filt), SUMSQ(y_filt))
  ))

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: SS_total (total sum of squares) as a scalar
functions.description:
SS_total is the total variation in Y before any predictors are added. With an intercept it equals the sum of squared deviations from the mean — DEVSQ(Y). Without an intercept it equals the raw sum of squares — SUMSQ(Y). It is the denominator in the R² formula and partitions into SS_regression + SS_residual.

Returns DEVSQ(filtered_Y) when Allow_Intercept is TRUE, SUMSQ(filtered_Y) when FALSE. Does not require X_s.

functions.name: SS_Residual
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    SS_Total(Y, allow_arg, filt_arg) * (1 - R_squared(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: SS_residual (residual/error sum of squares) as a scalar
functions.description:
SS_residual (also called SS_error) is the variation in Y left unexplained by the regression model — the sum of squared differences between observed and fitted values. It equals SS_total × (1 - R²) and shrinks as the model improves.

Computed as SS_Total(...) * (1 - R_squared(...)).

functions.name: SS_Regression
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    SS_Total(Y, allow_arg, filt_arg) * R_squared(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg)
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: SS_regression (explained/model sum of squares) as a scalar
functions.description:
SS_regression (also called SS_model or SS_explained) is the variation in Y explained by the regression model — the reduction in total variation achieved by adding the predictors. It equals SS_total × R² and grows as the model explains more.

Computed as SS_Total(...) * R_squared(...).

functions.name: SE_Regression
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    SQRT(SS_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg) / DF_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: SE_regression (standard error of the regression) as a scalar
functions.description:
SE_regression (also called the root mean square error or S) measures the typical distance between observed Y values and the regression line, in the same units as Y. It equals √(SS_residual / df_residual) = √MSE. Smaller values indicate a tighter fit.

Computed as SQRT(SS_Residual(...) / DF_Residual(...)).

functions.name: PRESS
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    e,         Residuals(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    h,         Hat_diagonal(X_s, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    SUMSQ(e / (1 - h))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: PRESS (Prediction Residual Error Sum of Squares) as a scalar
functions.description:
PRESS is the leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) sum of squared prediction errors. For each observation i the model is refitted on all other observations and evaluated at x_i; the shortcut formula avoids n separate refits by computing Σ(eᵢ / (1 − hᵢ))² where eᵢ are the OLS residuals and hᵢ are the hat-matrix diagonal (leverage) values.

Leverage is obtained from Hat_diagonal, which delegates the matrix inversion to Gram_Inverse. Then SUMSQ(e / (1 − h)) gives PRESS as a scalar.

functions.name: AIC
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    n,   Observations(Y, filt_arg),
    ssr, SS_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    p,   DF_Regression(X_s) + IF(allow_arg, 1, 0),
    n * LN(ssr / n) + 2 * p
  ))

functions.yields: Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) scalar
functions.description: AIC = n·ln(SSR/n) + 2p, where p = number of regression parameters (predictors + intercept when Allow_Intercept is TRUE). Smaller values indicate better-fitting models; compare across models on the same dataset.

functions.name: BIC
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    n,   Observations(Y, filt_arg),
    ssr, SS_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    p,   DF_Regression(X_s) + IF(allow_arg, 1, 0),
    n * LN(ssr / n) + p * LN(n)
  ))

arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) scalar
functions.description: BIC = n·ln(SSR/n) + p·ln(n), where p = number of regression parameters. Applies a heavier penalty than AIC for additional parameters, favouring sparser models in large samples.

functions.name: AICc
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    n,   Observations(Y, filt_arg),
    ssr, SS_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    p,   DF_Regression(X_s) + IF(allow_arg, 1, 0),
    aic, n * LN(ssr / n) + 2 * p,
    aic + 2 * p * (p + 1) / (n - p - 1)
  ))

functions.description: AICc = AIC + 2p(p+1)/(n−p−1). The small-sample correction reduces upward bias in AIC when n/p < 40. Converges to AIC as n → ∞.

functions.name: Durbin_Watson
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    e,         Residuals(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    SUM((DROP(e, 1) - DROP(e, -1))^2) / SUM(e^2)
  ))

arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: Durbin-Watson statistic as a scalar
functions.description:
DW = Σ(eₜ − eₜ₋₁)² / Σeₜ², testing for first-order serial correlation in residuals. Values near 2 indicate no autocorrelation; values below ~1.5 suggest positive autocorrelation, values above ~2.5 suggest negative autocorrelation.

Computed as SUM((DROP(e,1) − DROP(e,−1))²) / SUM(e²), where DROP(e,1) removes the first residual (giving e₂..eₙ) and DROP(e,−1) removes the last (giving e₁..eₙ₋₁), so consecutive differences are formed without OFFSET or index arithmetic.

functions.name: QQ_Correlation
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    sr,        Scaled_Residuals_Ranked(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    n,         ROWS(sr),
    ns,        NORM.S.INV((SEQUENCE(n) - 0.5) / n),
    CORREL(sr, ns)
  ))

functions.yields: Filliben Q-Q correlation coefficient (normality statistic) scalar
functions.description: CORREL(Scaled_Residuals_Ranked, Normal_Scores) — the Filliben approximation to the Shapiro-Wilk statistic. Values near 1 indicate approximately normal residuals; values below ~0.99 suggest non-normality. The Q-Q plot is the corresponding visual: plot Normal_Scores (x) vs Scaled_Residuals_Ranked (y) and look for alignment with the identity line.

functions.name: Coefficients
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    ls,        LINEST(FILTER(Y, filt_arg), FILTER(X_s, filt_arg), allow_arg, FALSE),
    k,         COLUMNS(X_s),
    TRANSPOSE(IF(allow_arg,
      HSTACK(INDEX(ls, 1, k + 1), CHOOSECOLS(ls, SEQUENCE(1, k, k, -1))),
      CHOOSECOLS(ls, SEQUENCE(1, k, k, -1))
    ))
  ))

Returns a vertical spill array of the fitted OLS regression coefficients. When Allow_Intercept is TRUE the intercept is the first element, followed by the coefficients for each column of X_s in input order. When Allow_Intercept is FALSE the output contains only the k predictor coefficients.

functions.name: VIF
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    filt_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    k,        COLUMNS(X_s),
    IF(k = 1,
      1,
      LET(
        col_idx, SEQUENCE(1, k),
        R2_vec,  MAKEARRAY(k, 1, LAMBDA(j, _,
          R_squared(
            CHOOSECOLS(X_s, FILTER(col_idx, col_idx <> j)),
            CHOOSECOLS(X_s, j),
            TRUE,
            filt_arg
          )
        )),
        1 / (1 - R2_vec)
      )
    )
  ))

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: k×1 column vector of VIF values, one per predictor (does not include an intercept row)
functions.description:
Variance Inflation Factor for each predictor Xⱼ = 1 / (1 − R²ⱼ), where R²ⱼ is the R² from regressing Xⱼ on all other predictors. VIF measures how much the variance of coefficient j is inflated by multicollinearity. VIF = 1 means no collinearity; VIF > 10 (or > 5 by stricter convention) signals a problem.

Auxiliary regressions always include an intercept regardless of the main model's Allow_Intercept setting (standard convention). When k = 1 the function returns 1 (no collinearity possible with a single predictor). Uses MAKEARRAY + FILTER to iterate over column indices without VBA or helper columns.

functions.description:
Tolerance = 1 − R²ⱼ = 1 / VIF, where R²ⱼ is the coefficient of determination from regressing Xⱼ on all other predictors. Values below 0.1 (VIF > 10) conventionally flag severe multicollinearity; values below 0.2 (VIF > 5) flag moderate concern.

Computed as 1 / VIF(...), forwarding all arguments.

functions.name: Prediction_Interval
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, X_new, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter], [alpha],
  LET(
    allow_arg,     IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,      IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    alpha_arg,     IF(ISOMITTED(alpha),           0.05, alpha),
    X_design,      Design_Matrix(X_s, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    beta,          Coefficients(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    s,             SE_Regression(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    df,            DF_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    t_crit,        T.INV.2T(alpha_arg, df),
    x_new_aligned, IF(allow_arg, X_new, INDEX(X_new, SEQUENCE(ROWS(X_new) - 1, 1, 2, 1))),
    XtX_inv,       Gram_Inverse(X_design),
    h_new,         MMULT(MMULT(TRANSPOSE(x_new_aligned), XtX_inv), x_new_aligned),
    point_est,     SUMPRODUCT(x_new_aligned, beta),
    se_pred,       s * SQRT(1 + h_new),
    margin,        t_crit * se_pred,
    VSTACK(
      point_est,
      se_pred,
      t_crit,
      point_est - margin,
      point_est + margin,
      1 - alpha_arg
    )
  ))

arguments.name: array

functions.yields: 1..n column vector of relative row numbers
functions.description:
Returns a 1-based integer sequence 1, 2, …, n where n = ROWS(array). The row numbers are relative to the top of the supplied array, so they are stable regardless of where the array sits on the sheet or whether it has been pre-filtered by the caller.

functions.name: Exclude_row_n
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(array, n,
  LET(
    total_rows, ROWS(array),
    n_abs,      IF(n < 0, total_rows + n + 1, n),
    IF(
      OR(n_abs < 1, n_abs > total_rows),
      NA(),
      LET(
        rows, SEQUENCE(total_rows),
        CHOOSEROWS(array, FILTER(rows, rows <> n_abs))
      )
    )
  )
)

functions.yields: array with row n removed; NA() if n is out of bounds
functions.description:
Returns the input array with exactly one row removed. Positive n selects from the top (1 = first row); negative n selects from the bottom (−1 = last row, −2 = second-to-last, …). Returns NA() when the resolved index is less than 1 or greater than ROWS(array).

Implemented as CHOOSEROWS(array, FILTER(SEQUENCE(total_rows), SEQUENCE(total_rows) <> n_abs)): SEQUENCE produces the full index 1..n, FILTER removes the target index, and CHOOSEROWS reassembles the array without that row.

functions.yields: scalar LOO prediction for observation n — the fitted value from a model trained on all rows except n, evaluated at row n of X_s
functions.description:
Applies the filter once in the outer scope to produce X_filt and Y_filt, then delegates to inner LAMBDAs without re-passing the filter. Exclude_row_n removes observation n from both X and Y; Coefficients fits OLS on the remaining n−1 rows; Design_Matrix builds the single-row design vector for row n (with or without intercept column); MMULT computes the dot product.

Note: for n LOO predictions at once use LOOCV_prediction, which avoids n separate OLS fits via the hat-matrix shortcut.

functions.name: LOOCV_prediction
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    yhat,      Predictions(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    e,         FILTER(Y, filt_arg) - yhat,
    h,         Hat_diagonal(X_s, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    yhat - h * e / (1 - h)
  )
)

functions.yields: n-element spill vector of LOO predictions for every filtered observation
functions.description:
Returns the leave-one-out predicted value for every observation simultaneously, without fitting n separate models. Uses the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury update: ŷ_{−i}(xᵢ) = ŷᵢ − hᵢ eᵢ / (1 − hᵢ), where ŷᵢ = Predictions, eᵢ = Y − ŷᵢ, and hᵢ is the hat-matrix diagonal from Hat_diagonal.

The LOOCV residual for each row equals eᵢ / (1 − hᵢ), so SUMSQ(LOOCV_residuals) = PRESS.

functions.name: Hat_diagonal
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    X_design,  Design_Matrix(X_s, allow_arg, filt_arg),
    p,         COLUMNS(X_design),
    XtX_inv,   Gram_Inverse(X_design),
    Z,         MMULT(X_design, XtX_inv),
    MMULT(Z * X_design, SEQUENCE(p, 1, 1, 0))
  ))

functions.description:
Wraps CHOOSECOLS to give column selection a named, self-documenting form. The output is a calculated array with the same row count as the source table, valid as X_s in any library function.

Primary use: define a named range — e.g. X_Predictors = Col_Select(LifeData, {3,7,9}) — then pass that name as X_s. Non-contiguous column sets are fully supported. Combine with Complete_Cases_Filter to drop rows that have missing or non-numeric values in the chosen columns.

functions.name: Complete_Cases_Filter

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column), or a Col_Select result

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range; when supplied, rows where Y is also non-numeric are excluded

functions.yields: boolean column vector — TRUE for rows where every included column is numeric
functions.description:
Produces a ready-made Filter argument for any library function. TRUE rows have no blanks, text, or errors in any of the supplied columns.

When Y is omitted, only X_s columns are checked. When Y is provided, it is HSTACKed onto X_s so that a single MMULT row-sum determines completeness across all regression inputs at once. ISNUMBER returns FALSE for errors and blanks, so error cells are safely treated as incomplete without propagating into the MMULT result.

=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Filter],
  LET(
    filt_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    xf, FILTER(X_s, filt_arg),
    yf, FILTER(Y,   filt_arg),
    MAKEARRAY(COLUMNS(X_s), 1, LAMBDA(r, c, CORREL(CHOOSECOLS(xf, r), yf)))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: predictor column range (single or multi-column); returns one correlation per column

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: k×1 column vector of Pearson correlations between each predictor and Y
functions.description:
Pearson_R computes the linear (Pearson product-moment) correlation between each column of X_s and Y, after applying the optional filter. When X_s has a single column the result is a scalar; when X_s has k columns it spills as a k×1 column vector.

A Pearson_R close to ±1 indicates a strong linear association. Comparing Pearson_R with Spearman_R on the same data reveals nonlinearity: a large gap (Spearman > Pearson in magnitude) suggests a monotonic but curved relationship that may warrant a log or polynomial transformation.

functions.name: Spearman_R
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Filter],
  LET(
    filt_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    xf, FILTER(X_s, filt_arg),
    yf, FILTER(Y,   filt_arg),
    ry, BYROW(yf, LAMBDA(v, RANK.AVG(v, yf, 1))),
    MAKEARRAY(COLUMNS(X_s), 1, LAMBDA(r, c,
      LET(col, CHOOSECOLS(xf, r),
          rx,  BYROW(col, LAMBDA(v, RANK.AVG(v, col, 1))),
          CORREL(rx, ry))))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: predictor column range (single or multi-column); returns one correlation per column

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: k×1 column vector of Spearman rank correlations between each predictor and Y
functions.description:
Spearman_R computes the rank (Spearman) correlation between each column of X_s and Y after filtering. Ties receive average ranks (RANK.AVG). Returns a k×1 vector when X_s has k columns.

Unlike Pearson_R, Spearman_R measures any monotonic relationship, not just linear ones. The diagnostic value of the pair is in their difference: if |Spearman_R| is noticeably larger than |Pearson_R| for the same predictor, the relationship is curved and a transformation (e.g. LOG) or a nonlinear term may improve model fit.

functions.name: Skewness
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, [Filter],
  LET(
    filt_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    xf, FILTER(X_s, filt_arg),
    MAKEARRAY(COLUMNS(X_s), 1, LAMBDA(r, c, SKEW(CHOOSECOLS(xf, r))))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range to summarize (single or multi-column); returns one value per column

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: k×1 column vector of sample skewness values (one per column of X_s)
functions.description:
Skewness returns the sample skewness (Fisher-Pearson standardized third moment) for each column of X_s after filtering. Uses Excel's SKEW function, which divides by (n-1)(n-2).

Interpretation: 0 = symmetric; positive = right tail (mean > median, common in counts and incomes); negative = left tail. |Skewness| > 1 typically signals that a log or square-root transformation would linearize relationships and stabilize regression residual variance. Compare with Kurtosis for a fuller picture of distributional shape.

functions.name: Kurtosis
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, [Filter],
  LET(
    filt_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    xf, FILTER(X_s, filt_arg),
    MAKEARRAY(COLUMNS(X_s), 1, LAMBDA(r, c, KURT(CHOOSECOLS(xf, r))))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range to summarize (single or multi-column); returns one value per column

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: k×1 column vector of excess kurtosis values (one per column of X_s)
functions.description:
Kurtosis returns the excess kurtosis for each filtered column of X_s. Uses Excel's KURT function (Fisher's excess kurtosis: kurtosis − 3, so a normal distribution returns 0).

Positive excess kurtosis (leptokurtic) indicates heavier tails and more extreme outliers than a normal distribution. Negative (platykurtic) indicates lighter tails. High kurtosis in a predictor or in regression residuals signals that OLS standard errors may be unreliable, and that robust standard errors or a different distributional assumption may be warranted.

functions.name: F_Stat
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    SS_Regression(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg) / DF_Regression(X_s) /
    (SS_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg) / DF_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: F-statistic for the overall regression model as a scalar
functions.description:
F_Stat returns the F-statistic for the omnibus test of the null hypothesis that all regression coefficients are simultaneously zero. It equals (MS_Regression / MS_Residual) = (SS_Regression / df_regression) / (SS_Residual / df_residual).

A large F-statistic (and correspondingly small P_Value_F) means the model explains significantly more variance than would be expected by chance. Note that a significant F does not guarantee that every individual predictor is significant — individual t-statistics (T_Stats) address that question. F_Stat appears in the ANOVA table on the Regression sheet; this function exposes it as a named reference for use in other formulas.

functions.name: P_Value_F
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, Y, [Allow_Intercept], [Filter],
  LET(
    allow_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Allow_Intercept), TRUE, Allow_Intercept),
    filt_arg,  IF(ISOMITTED(Filter),          TRUE, Filter),
    F.DIST.RT(
      F_Stat(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg),
      DF_Regression(X_s),
      DF_Residual(X_s, Y, allow_arg, filt_arg)
    )
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of predictors (single or multi-column)

arguments.name: Y
arguments.description: single-column outcome range

arguments.name: Allow_Intercept
arguments.description: TRUE/FALSE — fit intercept? Default TRUE

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: p-value for the overall F-test (right-tail probability of the F distribution)
functions.description:
P_Value_F returns the p-value for the overall model F-test: the probability of observing an F-statistic at least as large as F_Stat under the null hypothesis that all coefficients are zero. Computed as F.DIST.RT(F_Stat, df_regression, df_residual).

Conventionally, P_Value_F < 0.05 indicates that the model as a whole fits the data significantly better than a null model. This p-value appears in the Significance F column of the Regression sheet ANOVA table; this function exposes it for programmatic use.

functions.name: Correlation_Matrix
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(X_s, [Filter],
  LET(
    filt_arg, IF(ISOMITTED(Filter), TRUE, Filter),
    xf, FILTER(X_s, filt_arg),
    k,  COLUMNS(X_s),
    MAKEARRAY(k, k, LAMBDA(r, c, CORREL(CHOOSECOLS(xf, r), CHOOSECOLS(xf, c))))
  ))

arguments.name: X_s
arguments.description: column range of variables (single or multi-column); returns a k×k symmetric matrix

arguments.name: Filter
arguments.description: boolean array — TRUE includes the row, FALSE excludes it

functions.yields: k×k symmetric matrix of pairwise Pearson correlations (diagonal = 1)
functions.description:
Correlation_Matrix returns the k×k Pearson correlation matrix for all columns of X_s after filtering. Each cell [r, c] equals CORREL(column r, column c). The diagonal is always 1. The matrix is symmetric. Enter as a single formula and let it spill.

Use this to screen for multicollinearity before fitting a model: pairs with |r| > 0.7 are candidates for VIF investigation. High off-diagonal correlations indicate redundant predictors whose coefficients will be unstable and hard to interpret. For formal post-fit diagnostics, use VIF and Tolerance instead.
